2015_087_121515mtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session at 7:00 p.m. on December 15, 2015 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, with a packet built around the October 2015 Treasurer's Report and the first General Fund budget amendment of the 2015-16 fiscal year. Total disbursements in the period were $13,161,998.42, including $10,276,919.03 in check disbursements, $2,727,645.44 in outgoing wire transfers, $149,296.43 in P-Card purchases and $8,582.52 in ACH debits. Budget Amendment #1 proposed General Fund revenue of $139,930,708 against expenditures of $141,360,708, driven chiefly by a $2,120,000 increase in MPSERS UAAL funding and removal of the original budget's $3,000,000 budget-reduction assumption.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, regular meeting, 7:00 p.m., December 15, 2015, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
The 18th District Sons of the American Legion "Flags for Classrooms" program, chaired by Randy Jackson, presented 62 American flags to Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning Mark Dziatczak for Baker, Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools and Athens and Troy High. A TSD Mission Moment honored the Wattles and Troy Union WATCH D.O.G.S. (Dads of Great Students), including principals Joyce Brasington and Mike Cottone.

**Consent agenda (Item 5)**
Minutes of the November 10, 2015 Board workshop, the November 17, 2015 special workshop and the November 17, 2015 regular meeting; the October 2015 Treasurer's Report; and second reading and adoption of Board Policies E-1102 (Use of School Buildings and Facilities) and D-1401 (Reimbursement of Board Member and Employee Expenses).

**November 17 actions carried in the minutes**
Resolutions 15-098 through 15-104, each adopted Yes 6, No 0 with Mr. Miletti absent: a summer tax levy resolution continuing collection of one-half of school property taxes beginning with 2016 under 1976 P.A. 451; music instrument bids totaling $124,357.00; mechanical/electrical/plumbing awards of $5,986,790.00 at Athens High and $2,791,110.49 at Troy High from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; and a $100,000 Capital Maintenance Fund amendment. Rick West reported that the operating millage renewal passed November 3, 2015.

**Item 8.A — Budget Update (report only)**
Rick West's December 1, 2015 workshop deck showed General Fund revenue moving from an original $136,512,079 to $139,930,708 and expenditures from $137,945,141 to $141,360,708, with ending fund equity of $19,271,637, or 13.63% of expenditures. State funding rises 3.3% on a $2,120,000 MPSERS UAAL increase, $357,000 in special education funding, $173,000 in Hold Harmless categorical, $69,000 in vocational education and $106,000 tied to enrollment growth from 12,560 to 12,706 students.

**Items 8.B–8.D (consideration)**
Budget amendment appropriations of $141,360,708 (General Fund), $2,743,022 (Community Education Fund), $98,616,289 (2014 Capital Projects Fund) and $200,000 (Capital Maintenance Fund); notice of withdrawal from the MAISL insurance pool to seek property/casualty/liability bids beginning July 1, 2016; and award of roof assessment, design and consulting services through 2019 to WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc. per its May 21, 2015 bid, payable from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.

**Identification.** Board meeting agenda and packet of the Troy School District, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us), for the regular meeting of December 15, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition items.** Randy Jackson, chairman of the 18th District Sons of the American Legion "Flags for Classrooms" program, presented 62 American flags to Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning Mark Dziatczak for classrooms at Baker, Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools and at Athens High and Troy High; the program's goal is a flag in every classroom in Oakland County. A TSD Mission Moment recognized the Wattles and Troy Union WATCH D.O.G.S. (Dads of Great Students) volunteers, with certificates to Wattles Principal Joyce Brasington, Troy Union Interim Principal Mike Cottone, teachers Brad Sassack, Jamie VanHouzen and Patrick Werner, and parents Brian Corbett, Bob Schneeweis and Brendan Sennott.

**Consent agenda.** Item 5 covered minutes of the November 10, 2015 Board workshop, the November 17, 2015 special Board workshop and the November 17, 2015 Board meeting; the October 2015 Treasurer's Report; and second reading and adoption of Board Policy E-1102, Use of School Buildings and Facilities, and Board Policy D-1401, Reimbursement of Board Member and Employee Expenses.

**November minutes.** The November 10 workshop opened at 6:00 p.m. under President Philippart with Mrs. Edmunds, Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Schmidt and Ms. Underwood present and Mr. Miletti absent; Superintendent Machesky, administrators West, Carson, Pass, Dziatczak and Harris, and Bill Bowman of Great Northern Consulting Group attended for a property report, music equipment, mechanical/electrical/plumbing at Athens and Troy High, summer tax collection, October cash positions and a book study of "Who's AFRAID of the BIG BAD DRAGON?"; it adjourned at 9:37 p.m. The November 17 special workshop ran 6:15 p.m. to 6:58 p.m. with Dr. Wayne Peters of Neola, Inc. The November 17 regular meeting convened at 7:02 p.m. and adjourned at 8:05 p.m.; Larson Middle School Principal Joe Duda and science teacher Sandy Bammel presented the 8th Grade Stream Leaders program, sponsored by the Clinton River Watershed Council and begun at Larson in fall 2013. Secretary Paula Fleming submitted all three sets of minutes.

**November resolutions (all Yes 6, No 0, Miletti absent).** 15-098 approved the consent agenda. 15-099 approved personnel recommendations and a probationary contract for new hire Jennifer Locke. 15-100 named Jordan Harris chief spokesperson for TEA/MEA/NEA, TESA/MEA/NEA and TESPA/MEA/NEA bargaining, each contract expiring June 30, 2016, with Rick West, Mark Dziatczak, Kris Griffor, Dave Pass and, for two teams, Stephanie Maynard and Carmen White. Rick West reported the operating millage renewal passed November 3, 2015. 15-101 adopted the annual summer tax resolution to collect one-half of school property taxes, including debt service, beginning with 2016 under 1976 P.A. 451, with collection expenses negotiable under MCLA 380.1612 and delivery to the City of Troy required before January 1, 2016. 15-102 awarded music instrument bids of $124,357.00 from the Capital Projects Fund: Washington Music Center $92,010.00, Sam Ash Corporation $747.00, Brook Mays Music $31,600.00. 15-103 awarded mechanical and electrical upgrades from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund: Athens High School — Titan Ind. general trades $377,489.00, Ecker mechanical $4,301,000.00, Metro Electric electrical $1,308,300.00, total $5,986,790.00; Troy High School — Titan Ind. $239,610.49, Contrast mechanical $2,240,000.00, J & J Electric $311,500.00, total $2,791,110.49. 15-104 amended the Capital Maintenance Fund, moving fund balance July 1 from $701,919 to $729,355 and appropriating $100,000 of purchased services, with ending fund balance June 30 restated from $701,919 to $629,355. A second resolution numbered 15-104 approved Vice President Schmidt's attendance at the 2015 NAIS People of Color Conference in Tampa, Florida, December 3-5, 2015, under Board Policy B-2001.

**Policies.** E-1102 Use of School Buildings and Facilities authorizes the Superintendent to approve facility use under a Board-approved fee schedule, requires charges so taxpayer funds are not used to support non-school activities, and cross-references Policy K-1501; adopted February 16, 1976 and revised January 16, 1979, September 19, 1989, April 21, 1998 and November 17, 2015. D-1401 Reimbursement of Board Member or Employee Expenses lists nine pre-approved categories, covers air travel at coach rate and mileage at the IRS rate, bars reimbursement of spouse expenses, requires prior Board approval by resolution for out-of-state Board member meetings under B-2001, and cites Revised School Code MCL 380.1254; the adoption line is blank.

**Item 8.A - Budget Update.** Rick West's "Business Services Update" deck from the December 1, 2015 workshop compared audited 6/30/2015, original 6/30/2016 and Amendment #1 figures: projected revenue $136,589,446, $136,512,079 and $139,930,708 (2.50%); projected expenditures $137,267,824, $137,945,141 and $141,360,708 (2.48%); revenue under expenditures ($678,378), ($1,433,062) and ($1,430,000); beginning fund equity $21,380,015, $18,379,968 and $20,701,637; ending fund equity $20,701,637, $16,946,906 and $19,271,637; fund equity as a percent of expenditures 15.08%, 12.29% and 13.63%. Revenue by source moves local from $35,198,639 to $36,040,808 (2.4%, attributed to property tax values), state from $90,070,344 to $93,055,841 (3.3%), federal from $3,395,503 to $3,115,244 (-8.3%) and incoming transfers from $7,847,593 to $7,718,815 (-1.6%, on anticipated reduction in PA 18 revenue). The state increase comprises $2,120,000 in MPSERS UAAL, $357,000 in special education funding, $173,000 in Hold Harmless categorical (a $105 categorical to secure a $25 per pupil increase), $69,000 in vocational education and $106,000 from student count growth from 12,560 to 12,706. By object, benefits rise from $43,908,451 to $45,986,672, supplies fall from $6,392,270 to $5,926,683 after a $442,000 textbook reduction, capital outlay falls from $312,992 to $235,044, the ($3,000,000) budget reduction line is removed, and a positive variance of ($1,523,873) is added. MPSERS slides note the state portion at $675 million in FY 2014-15 rising to $908 million in FY 2015-16, with PA 300 of 2012 marking the rate-structure break. Fund schedules show Capital Projects ending fund balance moving from $27,104 to $139,918, Capital Maintenance from $701,919 to $529,355, and Community Education from $2,044,633 to $2,641,522; the timeline sets public hearing and millage rate adoption at the May/June Board meeting and budget adoption in June.

**Items 8.B, 8.C and 8.D.** The budget amendment resolution appropriates $141,360,708 for the General Fund, $2,743,022 for the Community Education Fund, $98,616,289 for the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and $200,000 for the Capital Maintenance Fund, with General Fund instruction rising to $94,864,698 (basic programs $78,875,270, added needs $15,263,889, adult/continuing education $725,539) and total support services to $46,427,118. Item 8.C recommends notifying MAISL of withdrawal from the Trust in order to consider additional property/casualty/liability insurance bids beginning July 1, 2016, in accordance with MAISL by-laws and without constituting a final decision. Item 8.D, following an RFP reviewed by Director of Maintenance and Operations Rob Carson and Owners Representative Michelle Kerns, authorizes a contract with WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc. for roof assessment, design and consulting services through 2019 consistent with its May 21, 2015 bid, as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund.
